## Maintainer ruling — 2026-08-12

**裁定:方向 B —— read/evaluate 保持开放,delete 需要平台级权限。**

要点:
- `deleteRule` 对 `organization_id = null` 的行,要求调用者持有平台级权限(`manage_platform_settings` 或 `platform_admin` 位置);仅持 org 级 `manage_sharing` 者拒绝。
- 错误面用 **403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`**,不是 404 —— 该行是有意可见的,404 会撒谎。
- #7760 开放的能力(列出、查看、评估种子规则)全部保持不动。
- 依据卡内两条实测:删除是「披着 removal 外衣的 revocation」(重启即复活、换 id),且安全杠杆(停用)对 org 管理员不可用而破坏杠杆反而可用 —— 这是反向的安全排布,收掉破坏杠杆是结构性修复。
- ⛔ **不做 D**(per-org 抑制机制):无任何实测需求。记录在案:本裁定落地后 org 管理员对平台级规则将没有任何杠杆;若未来出现真实的 per-org 抑制需求,另立卡评估,不预建。

裁定人:维护者 huangyiirene(2026-08-12,接受 PM 综合分析后批准);由 PM 会话 `session_01GZKbx4xyF7U5WXj6ch49BM` 代笔落卡。转 `pm:queue`。

## The ruling this executes (维护者 2026-08-12) — quoted verbatim, untranslated

> **裁定:方向 B —— read/evaluate 保持开放,delete 需要平台级权限。**
>
> - `deleteRule` 对 `organization_id = null` 的行,要求调用者持有平台级权限(`manage_platform_settings` 或 `platform_admin` 位置);仅持 org 级 `manage_sharing` 者拒绝。
> - 错误面用 **403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`**,不是 404 —— 该行是有意可见的,404 会撒谎。
> - #7760 开放的能力(列出、查看、评估种子规则)全部保持不动。
> - 依据卡内两条实测:删除是「披着 removal 外衣的 revocation」(重启即复活、换 id),且安全杠杆(停用)对 org 管理员不可用而破坏杠杆反而可用 —— 这是反向的安全排布,收掉破坏杠杆是结构性修复。
> - ⛔ **不做 D**(per-org 抑制机制):无任何实测需求。记录在案:本裁定落地后 org 管理员对平台级规则将没有任何杠杆;若未来出现真实的 per-org 抑制需求,另立卡评估,不预建。

## Three things in that ruling that are easy to under-implement

1. **403, not 404 — and the reason is load-bearing.** The row is *deliberately visible* (that is what #7760 opened), so a 404 would be a lie the platform tells about a row the caller can list and read one call earlier. ⛔ Do not "harden" it into a 404.
2. **#7760's read/evaluate surface stays open** — listing, viewing and evaluating seed rules are the regression surface, not collateral. A fix that gates the whole `organization_id = null` class rather than just `delete` reverses a shipped decision.
3. **⛔ Do not build direction D.** The ruling names the consequence it is knowingly accepting — after this lands, org admins have *no* lever over platform-level rules — and rules out pre-building a suppression mechanism. If the dev feels the absence of a lever is a gap, that is a **report**, not a rider.

## Premise re-verification is the dev's first action

This card was ruled at 03:04Z; `plugin-sharing` has taken **two** merges from this lane since (#8097 rewrote `expandRecipient` and `business-unit-graph.ts`; #8120 added `federated-phantom-anchors.ts` and guarded both filters). Neither should have touched `deleteRule`, but line anchors have drifted twice in this package today — locate by symbol, and confirm the two measurements the ruling rests on (delete-is-revocation: restart revives, id changes; and the disable lever being unavailable to org admins while the destructive one is available) still hold before building on them.

**PM review: ACCEPT** — PR #8156. Seat #6022, session `session_01PEVB6w7D7uCszR9Mw1BL73`. CI convergence is mine.

## Verified against GitHub

| check | result |
|:--|:--|
| Path face | ✅ 3 files, zero fork triggers |
| 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, not 404 | ✅ — and the test asserts the code is **not equal** to either 404-shaped code (`RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, `RULE_NOT_FOUND`), so a 404 regression fails as a *named different* assertion |
| ⛔ direction D absent | ✅ — the one "suppression" hit in the diff is a **comment declining it**: *"The ruling explicitly declines to pre-build a per-org suppression mechanism (「⛔ 不做 D」) absent measured demand — do not add one here."* |
| #7760's read surface | ✅ untouched and pinned as a regression surface |
| Changeset | ✅ |

## You measured both of the ruling's premises before building on them

The ruling rested on two claims from the card. You probed both, first, with predictions written down:

- **(a) delete is revocation wearing removal's clothes** — `id1 ≠ id2` after restart, `grants after reboot = 1`. The rule comes back under a new id with grants re-materialised.
- **(b) the safe lever is unavailable while the destructive one is not** — an org admin's `active: false` produced `[{org: null, active: true}, {org: "org1", active: false}]`, i.e. a *second, org-stamped* row while the shared rule keeps running; the delete, by contrast, worked.

⚠️ A ruling whose premises have quietly expired is worse than no ruling, because it still reads as authoritative. Confirming them costs one probe file and you deleted it after. That is the right shape.

## Assumption #3 — you didn't just answer it, you found the check it implies

I asked which mechanism to use, since the ruling names both `manage_platform_settings` and `platform_admin`. Your finding:

> they are **NOT synonyms** but two independent channels carrying the same unscoped `admin_full_access` grant onto `ExecutionContext` — the capability arrives on `systemPermissions`, the position on `positions` as a resolver-derived built-in. **A resolver-built context carries both; a hand-built one may carry only one.**

So the check accepts **either** — the fail-safe reading, since requiring both would refuse a legitimately-authorized caller whose context was assembled differently. And you **declined to widen to `PLATFORM_ADMIN_ONLY_CAPABILITIES`**, which would have authorized more than was ruled. That restraint is the part I would have had to catch, and you got there first.

## The guard's placement is a disclosure decision, and you made the right one

> the guard sits **AFTER** `getRule` resolves, so a row the caller cannot see keeps its existing silent no-op instead of gaining a refusal that would disclose it

Placing it before the lookup would have turned "this row does not exist for you" into "this row exists and you may not touch it" — leaking the existence of rows outside the caller's visibility, in a PR whose entire purpose is tightening a security boundary. Not mentioned in the ruling, correctly decided anyway.

## The docs question — no change, and the reason is a phrase collision worth recording

I flagged that a card *adding a refusal* has an inverted docs risk: if any page promises org admins this capability, the prose keeps promising a lever the ruling knowingly removes.

Three pages do contain "platform-global" — `sharing-rules.mdx:63`, `permissions-matrix.mdx:47`, `rls.mdx:84`. ⚠️ **All three use it in a different sense**: `tenancy.enabled: false`, an *object's* tenancy posture, not a *sharing rule* with `organization_id = null`. Nothing documents org-admin deletion of platform-global rules, so there is nothing to update.

Recording it because the collision is a live trap: the same phrase means two things in this repo, and a grep-and-glance review would have "found" a docs conflict that does not exist — the mirror image of the count-based false alarms this lane hit three times today.

## #8158

Filed unassigned and unlabelled, with reachability explicitly **not** measured and flagged as the first thing triage should settle. `adminOrgScope` falling open when the caller has no org id — reached on `CAPABILITY`, not just `SYSTEM_CTX` — is a cross-tenant read (and evaluate) of every tenant's sharing rules if constructible. ⛔ Grading is triage's channel; I am not pre-empting it, but I will name it in the round report because "same class as #7761 through a different door" is the kind of pattern that deserves to be seen next to its sibling.

The folded-in fixture correction is right too: an ADR-0111 D6 fixture whose `RULE_ADMIN` had no `organizationId` was incidentally authoring **platform-global** rules — a shape no org admin can create through the API. Adding the missing declaration keeps that test on its own subject instead of re-spelling it away.

## Next (mine)

Per-job gate conclusions, then flip ready → arm, in that order.

裁定接受的那个后果也被如实记进了 guard 的 docblock,没有被绕过:本 PR 之后,org 管理员对平台级规则**不再有任何操作杠杆**。read / list / evaluate(#7760 开放的面)完整保留,并有 pin 守着。
